[[File:Independent dominating.svg|thumb|upright=0.75|A graph with a minimum '''independent dominating set''' in red. There are 3 vertices in the set, and therefore the '''independent domination number''' <math>i(G)=3</math> (which is greater than the [[domination number]] <math>\gamma(G)=2</math>).]]
{{distinguish|text=the [[independence dominating set]], a set which dominates an independent set of a graph}}

In [[graph theory]], an '''independent dominating set''' for a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] <math>G = (V, E)</math> is a [[subset]] <math>D \subseteq V</math> that is both a [[dominating set]] and an [[Independent set (graph theory)|independent set]]; equivalently, it is a [[maximal independent set]].<ref name="goddard2013">{{citation
 | last1 = Goddard | first1 = Wayne
 | last2 = Henning | first2 = Michael A.
 | title = Independent domination in graphs: A survey and recent results
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | volume = 313
 | issue = 7
 | year = 2013
 | pages = 839–854
 | doi = 10.1016/j.disc.2012.11.031
 | issn = 0012-365X
 }}</ref>

The '''independent domination number''' <math>i(G)</math> of a graph <math>G</math> is the size of the smallest independent dominating set (equivalently, the smallest maximal independent set).<ref name="goddard2013"/> The notation <math>i(G)</math> was introduced by Cockayne and Hedetniemi.<ref name="cockayne1974">{{citation
 | last1 = Cockayne | first1 = E. J.
 | last2 = Hedetniemi | first2 = S. T.
 | title = Independence graphs
 | journal = Congressus Numerantium
 | volume = X
 | year = 1974
 | pages = 471–491
 }}</ref><ref name="cockayne1977">{{citation
 | last1 = Cockayne | first1 = E. J.
 | last2 = Hedetniemi | first2 = S. T.
 | title = Towards a theory of domination in graphs
 | journal = Networks
 | volume = 7
 | year = 1977
 | pages = 247–261
 | doi = 10.1002/net.3230070305
 }}</ref>

== History ==

The concept of an independent dominating set arose from [[chess problem]]s. In 1862, de Jaenisch posed the problem of finding the minimum number of mutually non-attacking [[queen (chess)|queens]] that can be placed on a chessboard so that every square is attacked by at least one queen.<ref name="dejaenisch">{{citation
 | last = de Jaenisch | first = C. F.
 | title = Traité des Applications de l'Analyse Mathématique au Jeu des Échecs
 | year = 1862
 }}</ref> Modelling the chessboard as a [[queen's graph]] <math>G</math>, this minimum is the independent domination number <math>i(G)</math>. For the standard 8×8 queens graph, <math>\alpha(G) = 8</math>, <math>i(G) = 7</math>, and <math>\gamma(G) = 5</math>.<ref name="goddard2013"/>

The theory of independent domination was formalized by [[Claude Berge|Berge]] and [[Oystein Ore|Ore]] in 1962.<ref name="berge1962">{{citation
 | last = Berge | first = Claude | author-link = Claude Berge
 | title = Theory of Graphs and its Applications
 | publisher = Methuen
 | location = London
 | year = 1962
 }}</ref><ref name="ore1962">{{citation
 | last = Ore | first = Oystein | author-link = Oystein Ore
 | title = Theory of graphs
 | journal = Amer. Math. Soc. Transl.
 | volume = 38
 | year = 1962
 | pages = 206–212
 }}</ref> Berge observed that an independent set is maximal independent if and only if it is dominating, and that every maximal independent set is a [[Dominating set#Minimal dominating sets|minimal dominating set]].<ref name="berge1962"/>

== Bounds ==

=== General bounds ===

Berge established basic bounds in terms of the [[order (graph theory)|order]] <math>n</math> and maximum [[degree (graph)|degree]] <math>\Delta</math> of a graph:<ref name="berge1973">{{citation
 | last = Berge | first = Claude | author-link = Claude Berge
 | title = Graphs and Hypergraphs
 | publisher = North-Holland
 | location = Amsterdam
 | year = 1973
 }}</ref>

:<math>\left\lceil \frac{n}{1+\Delta} \right\rceil \leq i(G) \leq n - \Delta</math>

For graphs without isolated vertices:<ref name="favaron1988">{{citation
 | last = Favaron | first = Odile
 | title = Two relations between the parameters of independence and irredundance
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | volume = 70
 | year = 1988
 | pages = 17–20
 | doi = 10.1016/0012-365X(88)90076-3
 }}</ref>

:<math>i(G) \leq n + 2 - 2\sqrt{n}</math>

and this bound is sharp. For a graph with minimum degree at least <math>\delta</math>:<ref name="sunwang1999">{{citation
 | last1 = Sun | first1 = Liang
 | last2 = Wang | first2 = Jianfang
 | title = An upper bound for the independent domination number
 | journal = Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B
 | volume = 76
 | year = 1999
 | pages = 240–246
 | doi = 10.1006/jctb.1999.1907
 }}</ref>

:<math>i(G) \leq n + 2\delta - 2\sqrt{\delta n}</math>

confirming an earlier conjecture of Favaron.<ref name="favaron1988"/>

=== Graph families ===

For [[claw-free graph]]s:<ref name="allan1978">{{citation
 | last1 = Allan | first1 = Robert B.
 | last2 = Laskar | first2 = Renu
 | title = On domination and independent domination numbers of a graph
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | volume = 23
 | year = 1978
 | pages = 73–76
 | doi = 10.1016/0012-365X(78)90105-X
 | issue = 2
 | doi-access = free
 }}</ref>

:<math>i(G) = \gamma(G)</math>

More generally, for <math>K_{1,k}</math>-free ([[star (graph theory)|star]]-free) graphs where <math>k \geq 3</math>:<ref name="bollobas1979">{{citation
 | last1 = Bollobás | first1 = Béla | author1-link = Béla Bollobás
 | last2 = Cockayne | first2 = E. J.
 | title = Graph-theoretic parameters concerning domination, independence, and irredundance
 | journal = Journal of Graph Theory
 | volume = 3
 | year = 1979
 | pages = 241–249
 | doi = 10.1002/jgt.3190030306
 }}</ref>

:<math>i(G) \leq (k-2)\gamma(G) - (k-3)</math>

For any [[bipartite graph]] without isolated vertices on <math>n</math> vertices:<ref name="goddard2013"/>
:<math>i(G) \leq n/2</math>

For [[tree (graph theory)|trees]], if a tree has <math>n</math> vertices and <math>\ell</math> leaves:<ref name="favaron1992">{{citation
 | last = Favaron | first = Odile
 | title = A bound on the independent domination number of a tree
 | journal = Vishwa International Journal of Graph Theory
 | volume = 1
 | year = 1992
 | pages = 19–27
 }}</ref>
:<math>i(G) \leq (n + \ell)/3</math>

If <math>G</math> is an <math>r</math>-[[regular graph]] on <math>n</math> vertices with no isolated vertex, then:<ref name="rosenfeld1964">{{citation
 | last = Rosenfeld | first = M.
 | title = Independent sets in regular graphs
 | journal = Israel Journal of Mathematics
 | volume = 2
 | year = 1964
 | pages = 262–272
 | doi = 10.1007/BF02759743
 }}</ref>
:<math>i(G) \leq \alpha(G) \leq n/2</math>

For [[connectivity (graph theory)|connected]] [[cubic graph]]s other than <math>K_{3,3}</math>:<ref name="lam1999">{{citation
 | last1 = Lam | first1 = P. C. B.
 | last2 = Shiu | first2 = W. C.
 | last3 = Sun | first3 = L.
 | title = On independent domination number of regular graphs
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | volume = 202
 | year = 1999
 | pages = 135–144
 | doi = 10.1016/S0012-365X(98)00350-1
 }}</ref>
:<math>i(G) \leq 2n/5</math>

It has been conjectured that the bound can be improved to <math>3n/8</math> for all connected cubic graphs of order more than 10.<ref name="goddard2013"/>

Regarding the ratio between domination and independent domination in connected cubic graphs other than <math>K_{3,3}</math>:<ref name="southey2012">{{citation
 | last1 = Southey | first1 = J.
 | last2 = Henning | first2 = M. A.
 | title = Domination versus independent domination in cubic graphs
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | year = 2013
 | doi = 10.1016/j.disc.2012.01.003
 }}</ref>
:<math>i(G)/\gamma(G) \leq 4/3</math>

For any [[planar graph]] on <math>n</math> vertices:<ref name="macgillivray2004">{{citation
 | last1 = MacGillivray | first1 = G.
 | last2 = Seyffarth | first2 = K.
 | title = Bounds for the independent domination number of graphs and planar graphs
 | journal = Journal of Combinatorial Mathematics and Combinatorial Computing
 | volume = 49
 | year = 2004
 | pages = 33–55
 }}</ref>
:<math>i(G) \leq 3n/4 - 2</math>

For planar graphs of [[Distance (graph theory)|diameter]] 2, the bound can be improved:<ref name="macgillivray2004"/>
:<math>i(G) \leq \lceil n/3 \rceil</math>

=== Relation to line graphs and edge domination ===

For any graph <math>G</math>, its [[line graph]] <math>L(G)</math> is claw-free, and hence a minimum maximal independent set in <math>L(G)</math> is also a minimum dominating set in <math>L(G)</math>. An independent set in <math>L(G)</math> corresponds to a [[Matching (graph theory)|matching]] in <math>G</math>, and a dominating set in <math>L(G)</math> corresponds to an [[edge dominating set]] in <math>G</math>. Therefore a [[minimum maximal matching]] has the same size as a minimum edge dominating set.

=== Relation to other domination parameters ===

Because the minimum is taken over fewer sets (only the independent dominating sets are considered), <math>\gamma(G) \leq i(G)</math> for all graphs <math>G</math>. Similarly, since every maximal independent set is an independent set, <math>i(G) \leq \alpha(G)</math>, where <math>\alpha(G)</math> is the [[independence number]]. Furthermore, since every maximal independent set is a minimal dominating set, <math>\alpha(G) \leq \Gamma(G)</math>, where <math>\Gamma(G)</math> is the [[upper dominating set|upper domination number]] (the maximum size of a minimal dominating set). This yields the '''domination chain''':<ref name="cockayne1978">{{citation
 | last1 = Cockayne | first1 = E. J.
 | last2 = Hedetniemi | first2 = S. T.
 | last3 = Miller | first3 = D. J.
 | title = Properties of hereditary hypergraphs and middle graphs
 | journal = Canadian Mathematical Bulletin
 | volume = 21
 | year = 1978
 | pages = 461–468
 | doi = 10.4153/CMB-1978-079-5
 }}</ref>

:<math>\gamma(G) \leq i(G) \leq \alpha(G) \leq \Gamma(G).</math>

The inequality can be strict; there are graphs <math>G</math> for which <math>\gamma(G) < i(G)</math>. For example, let <math>G</math> be the ''double star graph'' consisting of vertices <math>x_1, \ldots, x_p, a, b, y_1, \ldots, y_q</math>, where <math>p, q > 1</math>. The edges of <math>G</math> are defined as follows: each <math>x_i</math> is adjacent to <math>a</math>, <math>a</math> is adjacent to <math>b</math>, and <math>b</math> is adjacent to each <math>y_j</math>. Then <math>\gamma(G) = 2</math> since <math>\{a, b\}</math> is a smallest dominating set. If <math>p \leq q</math>, then <math>i(G) = p + 1</math> since <math>\{x_1, \ldots, x_p, b\}</math> is a smallest dominating set that is also independent (it is a smallest maximal independent set).

However, the bounds <math>\gamma(G) \leq i(G) \leq \alpha(G)</math> are simultaneously sharp for the [[corona product|corona]] <math>H \circ K_1</math> of any graph <math>H</math>, which satisfies <math>\gamma(G) = i(G) = \alpha(G) = |V(H)|</math>.<ref name="goddard2013"/>

Cockayne and Mynhardt characterized which sequences of values are achievable:<ref name="cockayne1993">{{citation
 | last1 = Cockayne | first1 = E. J.
 | last2 = Mynhardt | first2 = C. M.
 | title = The sequence of upper and lower domination, independence and irredundance numbers of a graph
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | volume = 122
 | year = 1993
 | pages = 89–102
 | doi = 10.1016/0012-365X(93)90288-5
 }}</ref> A sequence <math>(s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4)</math> of integers is realizable as <math>(\gamma(G), i(G), \alpha(G), \Gamma(G))</math> for some graph <math>G</math> if and only if <math>1 \leq s_1 \leq s_2 \leq s_3 \leq s_4</math>, <math>s_1 = 1</math> implies <math>s_2 = 1</math>, and <math>s_3 = 1</math> implies <math>s_4 = 1</math>.

== Computational complexity ==

Determining whether <math>i(G) \leq k</math> for a given graph <math>G</math> and integer <math>k</math> is [[NP-complete]] in general,<ref name="garey1979">{{citation
 | last1 = Garey | first1 = Michael R. | author1-link = Michael Garey
 | last2 = Johnson | first2 = David S. | author2-link = David S. Johnson
 | title = Computers and Intractability
 | publisher = Freeman
 | location = New York
 | year = 1979
 }}</ref> and remains NP-complete even when restricted to [[bipartite graph]]s, [[line graph]]s, [[circle graph]]s, [[unit disk graph]]s, or [[planar graph|planar]] [[cubic graph]]s.<ref name="goddard2013"/> Furthermore, Irving showed that there is no polynomial-time algorithm to approximate the independent domination number within a constant factor unless [[P versus NP problem|P = NP]].<ref name="irving1991">{{citation
 | last = Irving | first = R. W.
 | title = On approximating the minimum independent dominating set
 | journal = Information Processing Letters
 | volume = 37
 | year = 1991
 | pages = 197–200
 | doi = 10.1016/0020-0190(91)90188-N
 }}</ref>

On the other hand, the independent domination number can be computed in linear time for [[tree (graph theory)|trees]]<ref name="beyer1977">{{citation
 | last1 = Beyer | first1 = T.
 | last2 = Proskurowski | first2 = A.
 | last3 = Hedetniemi | first3 = S.
 | last4 = Mitchell | first4 = S.
 | title = Independent domination in trees
 | journal = Congressus Numerantium
 | volume = XIX
 | year = 1977
 | pages = 321–328
 }}</ref> and in polynomial time for [[chordal graph]]s<ref name="farber1982">{{citation
 | last = Farber | first = Martin
 | title = Independent domination in chordal graphs
 | journal = Operations Research Letters
 | volume = 1
 | year = 1982
 | pages = 134–138
 | doi = 10.1016/0167-6377(82)90015-3
 }}</ref> and [[cocomparability graph]]s.<ref name="kratsch1993">{{citation
 | last1 = Kratsch | first1 = Dieter
 | last2 = Stewart | first2 = Lorna
 | title = Domination of cocomparability graphs
 | journal = SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics
 | volume = 6
 | year = 1993
 | pages = 400–417
 | doi = 10.1137/0406032
 }}</ref>

== Domination-perfect graphs ==

A graph <math>G</math> is called a '''domination-perfect graph''' if <math>\gamma(H) = i(H)</math> in every [[induced subgraph]] <math>H</math> of <math>G</math>.<ref name="sumnermoore1979">{{citation
 | last1 = Sumner | first1 = D. P.
 | last2 = Moore | first2 = J. L.
 | title = Domination perfect graphs
 | journal = Notices of the American Mathematical Society
 | volume = 26
 | year = 1979
 | pages = A-569
 }}</ref> Since an induced subgraph of a claw-free graph is claw-free, it follows that every claw-free graph is also domination-perfect.<ref name="faudree">{{citation
 | last1 = Faudree | first1 = Ralph | author1-link = Ralph Faudree
 | last2 = Flandrin | first2 = Evelyne
 | last3 = Ryjáček | first3 = Zdeněk
 | doi = 10.1016/S0012-365X(96)00045-3
 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = Discrete Mathematics
 | pages = 87–147
 | title = Claw-free graphs — A survey
 | volume = 164
 | year = 1997
 | mr = 1432221
 | doi-access = free
 }}</ref>

By a result of Sumner and Moore, a graph is domination perfect if and only if <math>\gamma(H) = i(H)</math> for every induced subgraph <math>H</math> with <math>\gamma(H) = 2</math>.<ref name="sumnermoore1979"/> Zverovich and Zverovich gave a complete characterization: a graph is domination perfect if and only if it contains none of seventeen specific graphs as an induced subgraph.<ref name="zverovich1995">{{citation
 | last1 = Zverovich | first1 = I. E.
 | last2 = Zverovich | first2 = V. E.
 | title = An induced subgraph characterization of domination perfect graphs
 | journal = Journal of Graph Theory
 | volume = 20
 | year = 1995
 | pages = 375–395
 | doi = 10.1002/jgt.3190200313
 }}</ref>

== Well-covered graphs ==

A graph is [[well-covered graph|well-covered]] if <math>i(G) = \alpha(G)</math>, that is, every maximal independent set is a maximum independent set. The concept was introduced by Plummer.<ref name="plummer1970">{{citation
 | last = Plummer | first = Michael D. | author-link = Michael D. Plummer
 | title = Some covering concepts in graphs
 | journal = Journal of Combinatorial Theory
 | volume = 8
 | year = 1970
 | pages = 91–98
 | doi = 10.1016/S0021-9800(70)80011-4
 }}</ref> Ravindra characterized the well-covered bipartite graphs: a connected bipartite graph is well-covered if and only if it contains a [[perfect matching]] <math>M</math> such that for every edge <math>uv \in M</math>, the subgraph induced by <math>N[u] \cup N[v]</math> is a [[complete bipartite graph]].<ref name="ravindra1977">{{citation
 | last = Ravindra | first = G.
 | title = Well-covered graphs
 | journal = Journal of Combinatorial Information and System Sciences
 | volume = 2
 | year = 1977
 | pages = 20–21
 }}</ref> As a consequence, a tree is well-covered if and only if it is <math>K_1</math> or the [[corona product|corona]] of a tree.<ref name="goddard2013"/>
